A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Reparameterization Proximal Policy Optimization by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original training curves, deterministic and stochastic evaluations on five control tasks, and component and hyperparameter ablations in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on the same five tasks, including GI-PPO comparisons and revised ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices B and E.

M1.justification: The stated objective changes from an importance-ratio-clipped objective in v1 Equation 8 to a surrogate objective with separate gradient clipping in v2 Equations 8 and 10. This is a limited objective-formulation revision: the operative gradient rule, action regeneration, caching, regularizers, and critic procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Hopper, Ant, Humanoid, and Anymal locomotion in DFlex and Hand Reorient manipulation in Rewarped. Appendix A retains the same environments, task requirements, state/action dimensions, and rewards. Expanded ablations vary algorithm settings within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GI-PPO, a directly relevant hybrid RPG/PPO method, throughout the five-task training comparison and deterministic and stochastic result tables. v1 discusses GI-PPO only as related work. PPO, SHAC, and SAPO remain evaluated, substantially extending comparison against prior sample-reuse methods.

E3.justification: Reported RPO settings change: Hopper entropy/KL coefficients move from 0.2/0.4 to 0.25/0.2, and Ant entropy from 0.5 to 0.35. v2 also specifies GI-PPO settings and replaces separate SAPO schedule/critic controls with a joint control. The existing tasks, horizon, parallel-environment counts, and 128-episode evaluations remain.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix C.3/Figure 6 separately tests exponential learning-rate decay and 32 critic updates for SAPO on Humanoid. v2 Appendix E/Figure 5 replaces these with a combined setting across all five tasks. This substantially broadens the hyperparameter-control analysis while removing isolation of the two factors. The three main RPO component ablations remain.

E5.justification: v1 specifies 12 random seeds. v2 newly specifies two runs per seed, giving 24 effective runs except in deterministic Hopper, to account for simulator stochasticity; the independent seed count remains 12. Figure 1 also identifies its comparison as using the same seed. Mean and standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 revises main and ablation scores and curves, adds GI-PPO results, and reports the expanded SAPO controls. For example, RPO's deterministic Humanoid result changes from 9035.38 ± 265.98 to 8958.41 ± 373.64. In stochastic Hopper, newly added GI-PPO scores 5512.30 versus RPO's 5469.33, changing the leading comparator. These are revised evaluations with changed settings or run reporting, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix D adds Proposition 1 and a change-of-variables proof of the importance-weighted off-policy surrogate-gradient estimator's unbiasedness, including Gaussian invertibility conditions and a multidimensional argument. v1 provides only a shorter Monte Carlo explanation. v2 also revises the mathematical characterization of clipping from an objective to a gradient operation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the claim of optimizing a tailored clipped surrogate objective with applying tailored clipping to the surrogate's policy gradient. The central claims about the BPTT connection, stable sample reuse, compatibility with variance reduction, and strong sample efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v2 localizes clipping's benefit to early training and explains it through initially large importance ratios approaching one during convergence. It also explains why clipping is inactive on the first update. Appendix E explicitly attributes the advantage over jointly adjusted SAPO to RPO's algorithmic design. These refine the earlier, broader stability explanations.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents GI-PPO's source implementation, double-critic architecture, AdamW/SiLU modifications, tuning, and dedicated hyperparameters. RPO coefficient disclosures are revised. Conversely, v2 removes the previously tabulated actor log-standard-deviation bounds, reducing one aspect of reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Heess et al.'s stochastic value gradients, Grimmett and Stirzaker, and Kullback and Leibler. It distinguishes its behavior-policy value objective from SVG and replaces earlier GI-PPO criticisms with a potential gradient-conflict argument. Most related-work coverage remains; consolidating the duplicate SAPO reference is bibliographic.

P1.justification: The separate theoretical-connection and algorithm sections are extensively reorganized into a unified Section 4 with staged gradient derivation, objective, regularization, and update subsections. Method explanations are substantially rewritten, ablation discussion is compressed, the appendix control study moves to Appendix E, and an LLM editing disclosure is added.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 2 and 3 become one redrawn three-panel schematic in v2. Figure 1 is resized and wrapped into the introduction; training plots gain GI-PPO; the appendix control plot expands into five panels. Tables gain GI-PPO rows, a comparison column, and a dedicated hyperparameter table, with substantial rearrangement.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens justification of the central contribution through the revised clipping formulation, Appendix D's explicit proof, direct GI-PPO comparisons, and broader SAPO controls. These address important theoretical and empirical support gaps in v1. The gains outweigh localized drawbacks: omitted variance bounds, loss of separate SAPO controls, and Appendix B's blanket best-results statement overlooking GI-PPO's higher stochastic Hopper mean.
